name: Domnall

was sent to the lands of Domnall Míldemail

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Domnall (Donal) is an Irish or Scottish hero. The name is popular in both Irish and Scottish tradition. Many minor heroes and kings carried it. The most important was Domnall of Tara. He succeeded the mad king Suibhne. Domnall Míldemail was a Scottish king. Cúchulainn came to his lands. The father of Cúchulainn's bride Emer sent him there, fearing for his daughter's virtue.

okr.objective: Record Domnall as a popular Irish or Scottish hero name carried by several kings.
key_results: Domnall is a name shared by many Irish and Scottish heroes and kings.
Domnall of Tara succeeded the mad king Suibhne.
Domnall Míldemail was the Scottish king who received the hero Cúchulainn.
Cúchulainn was sent there by the father of his bride Emer.
